STEEL STRIPS WHEELS – PLANS ₹1,400 CR GREENFIELD CAPEX
Expansion & Capacity Update

Capex Details
- In-principle Board approval received for Maharashtra greenfield facility.
- Total proposed investment stands at ₹1,400 Cr over 60 months.
- Alloy wheels: ₹815 Cr for 2.5 million units annually.
- Steel wheels: ₹410 Cr for 1.8 million units annually.
- Hot stamping: ₹175 Cr for 1.3 million strokes annually.
- Funding through debt and internal accruals.
- Project remains subject to approvals and clearances.

Growth Drivers
- Management expects alloy-wheel market growth of 12% annually.
- Steel-wheel market growth estimated at 4% annually.
- Bhuj expansion adds 1.2 million alloy-wheel capacity.
- Aluminium-knuckle capacity at Bhuj to increase by 0.6 million units.
- H1FY27 steel-wheel capacity utilisation reached 85%.
- Alloy-wheel capacity utilisation stood at 89%.
- FY27 alloy-wheel capacity target stands at approximately 6.2 million units.
- Hot stamping adds passenger-vehicle structural body-part manufacturing capabilities.

Key Monitorables
- Regulatory approvals and project execution timelines.
- Phased capex deployment and funding mix.
- Capacity commissioning and customer ramp-up.
- Incremental ROCE and profitability from new capacities.
- Balance-sheet impact from debt-funded expansion.

Key Takeaway
- Expansion targets higher-margin alloy wheels and product diversification.
- Strong existing utilisation supports the need for additional capacity.
- Returns depend on execution, demand and capacity utilisation.
- Debt levels and incremental ROCE remain critical monitorables.
- No Recommendations.

SPECIALISED CHEMICAL – CAPACITY CONSTRAINTS MEET STRONG DEMAND
Business & Investment Analysis

Business Overview
- Specialised chemical used in ceramic catalyst manufacturing.
- Material burns away, leaving precisely structured ceramic pores.
- End applications include diesel exhaust emission-control systems.
- Only two global manufacturers reportedly hold required approvals.
- One manufacturer is reportedly based in Ankleshwar, Gujarat.

Growth Catalysts
- European regulations mandate improved heavy-truck emission-control systems.
- Regulatory changes could drive catalyst demand from 2029.
- Sales increased 32% in the previous financial year.
- Half-year sales growth accelerated to 60%.

Capacity Constraints
- Management estimates revenue capacity at ₹850–900 Cr.
- Current annualised revenue has reached approximately ₹869 Cr.
- Existing manufacturing facilities are approaching capacity limits.
- New plant commissioning is expected around April 2028.

Key Risks
- One customer contributes 35% of total revenue.
- Operating cash conversion remains weak.
- Only around one-third of operating profit converted into cash.
- Capacity constraints could limit near-term growth.
- Expansion delays could restrict demand fulfilment.

Key Takeaway
- Regulatory demand creates a potential long-term growth opportunity.
- Capacity expansion timing is critical for growth realisation.
- Customer concentration and cash conversion require close monitoring.
- Exact chemical identity and company require further verification.
- Impact: Potentially Positive, Execution-Dependent

CHEMCON SPECIALITY CHEMICALS Q2 FY27

• Net Profit ₹7.52 Cr ↑30.84% YoY, ↓31.41% QoQ

CHEMBOND CHEMICALS Q2 CONCALL

• Strong revenue growth momentum expected to continue in H2 FY27.

• Q4 FY27 expected to benefit from historically strong seasonal demand.

• ₹1,000 Cr revenue ambition reiterated, supported by organic expansion and potential acquisitions.

• Raw material cost pressure expected to continue in Q3 at levels similar to Q2.

• EBITDA margin at 8.8% vs approximately 16.2% QoQ, impacted by higher material costs.

• Margin recovery expected within 1–2 quarters after raw material costs and supply chains normalize.

• Water Technologies revenue up 28% YoY in H1, supported by strong industrial demand.

• Water treatment chemical volumes up approximately 44% YoY.

• Data center water treatment business expanding, with customers including NTT, Yotta and CtrlS.

• New-age industries' contribution to Water Technologies revenue targeted to rise to 12–15% over three years from 7–8% currently.

• Construction Chemicals revenue up 30% YoY in H1, with increasing focus on sealants.

• Chemical Distribution revenue up 86% YoY, while Cleaning & Hygiene business grew 59% in H1.

• Equipment order book stands at approximately ₹15–20 Cr for FY27, with recurring chemical consumables supporting revenue visibility.

• Management evaluating synergistic acquisitions, with no major manufacturing capacity constraints for future expansion.

• Key risks include raw material inflation, fixed-price public sector contracts, delayed margin recovery and acquisition execution.

KOTAK MAHINDRA BANK Q2 FY27 CONCALL

• Long-term loan growth targeted at 1.5–2× nominal GDP growth.

• Core advances up 19% YoY, excluding FCNR-backed loans and KMIL portfolio transfer.

• Mobilised ₹55,344 Cr through FCNR-B deposits, with remaining liquidity to be deployed over coming quarters.

• NIM at 4.31% vs 4.53% QoQ, impacted by approximately 15 bps from FCNR-B-related transactions.

• NIM recovery expected from loan repricing and liquidity deployment, with greater benefits anticipated in Q4.

• Approximately 65–70% of the loan portfolio is floating-rate, supporting repricing benefits.

• Credit cost declined to 35 bps from 46 bps QoQ, reflecting disciplined underwriting.

• Gross NPA at 1.04% vs 1.18% QoQ, while Net NPA declined to 0.24%.

• CASA ratio excluding FCNR-B improved to 41.8% from 40.3% QoQ.

• SME advances up 27% YoY to approximately ₹1.4 lakh Cr, remaining a key growth priority.

• Corporate banking advances up 25% YoY, while fee income grew 36%.

• Gradual expansion of unsecured retail lending planned, with focus on existing customers and credit quality.

• Technology spending expected at around 13% of operating expenses, focused on AI, automation and cost efficiency.

• ECL transition expected to have a one-time impact below 2% of net worth; earlier estimates indicated 12–15 bps additional recurring credit cost, subject to regulatory clarity.

• Key risks include FCNR-B liquidity deployment, NIM pressure, rural credit risks, ECL transition and capital market volatility.

PERMANENT MAGNETS Q2 CONCALL

• FY27 revenue growth guidance at 20–30%, supported by EV demand and export orders.

• FY27 EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 20–25% vs approximately 25% in Q2.

• Automotive revenue ₹24 Cr ↑129% YoY, driven by strong export EV demand.

• EV demand expected to remain near Q2 levels through H2 FY27.

• Alloys revenue targeted at ₹40–50 Cr in FY27, with improved capacity utilisation expected in H2.

• Alloys revenue could reach ₹70–80 Cr in FY28, subject to successful capacity ramp-up.

• Alloys business expected to achieve EBITDA breakeven or marginally positive margins in FY27.

• Relay pilot supplies expected in H2 FY27, with commercialisation targeted for FY28.

• Relay business offers potential gross margins of 15–30%, subject to customer approvals and execution.

• Quantum Magnetics Phase 2 commissioned in October 2026, with commercial ramp-up expected in FY28, subject to approvals.

• Quantum Magnetics FY28 revenue potential indicated at ₹10–40 Cr, without firm management guidance.

• Quantum Phase 2 installed capacity has indicative annual revenue potential of ₹40–60 Cr, depending on product mix.

• ECMS approval received for incentives equivalent to 25% of eligible capex, subject to scheme conditions.

• Plant consolidation could generate annual savings of ₹5 Cr over time.

• Key risks include EV demand sustainability, alloys utilisation, relay approval delays, quantum commercialisation and dependence on Chinese imports.

TATACHEM : KENYA HIGH COURT SAYS NO JURISDICTION IN MAGADI DISPUTE

• High Court of Kenya order dated October 23, 2026 holds the court has no jurisdiction on the dispute and cannot take further steps
• Tata Chemicals Magadi (TCML), the Kenyan subsidiary, is examining the order and will take legal and all other necessary steps
• Committee led by the Principal Secretary for Mining and TCML's CEO is doing a detailed technical review and will report to the Cabinet Secretary
• Review to help establish a sustainable framework for responsible mining, value addition, community development and partnerships
• Follows the Ministry of Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs notice dated July 28, 2026 to TCML
Impact: Positive (No adverse ruling from the Kenya High Court; matter shifts to the technical review and legal route)

JAIPURKURT : OPENS 5TH STORE IN OCTOBER AT LUDHIANA

• New Jaipur Kurti store at Model Town, Ludhiana, the brand's second outlet in the city
• Follows four store openings in a single day earlier in October, taking the month's total to five
• October openings: Pacific Mall Jaipur, DT Mega Mall Gurugram, Apsara Road Jammu, Rajouri Garden Delhi, Model Town Ludhiana

• Disbursal API from the bank's side suspended after the fraudulent debits were identified; complaints being filed with cybercrime and law enforcement authorities
• No disruption to business operations identified
Impact: Negative (repeat cyber fraud with ₹7.27 Cr exposure; recovery uncertain and controls around the API disbursal engine appear weak)

eMudhra's decision to exit its global website security certificate business following a cryptographic key generation failure raises some serious questions. 

Eight intermediate certificate authorities were left vulnerable because the generated keys were weaker than intended. The output wasn't reviewed after the ceremony, and the company attributed the failure to a script error and human oversight.

For a company built around digital trust and security, this is more than just a technical glitch. When your entire business revolves around trust, even one lapse in execution can have serious consequences. 

The bigger questions are around internal controls, quality assurance, risk management and management oversight.

- Adani Green Energy (ADANIGREEN): Grid availability reportedly falls below 80% due to expansion delays, forcing production curtailment. Report remains unverified.

- Indosolar (INDOSOLAR): Q2 EBITDA falls 79% YoY to ₹14.8 Cr; margin at 9.5%. Module sales decline to 98 MW; merger with Waaree Energies proposed.

- Container Corporation of India (CONCOR): Receives ~₹5.9 Cr GST demand for FY19. Company plans appeal and sees no material impact.

- Unifinz Capital: Reports ₹7.7 Cr cyber fraud through 346 unauthorised transactions. Account frozen; cybercrime complaint filed.

- AMD Industries (AMDIND): CFO Sanjeev Kumar Singhal resigns effective October 21, citing personal reasons.

- Star Paper Mills (STARPAPER): Receives ~₹1.5 Cr GST demand for FY24. Appeal planned; no material impact expected.

- Swiggy (SWIGGY): Motilal Oswal cuts target amid delayed profitability. Food delivery growth guidance remains 18–20%.

- Orient Cement (ORIENTCEM): Q2 PAT falls 35% to ₹32 Cr from ₹49 Cr.

- Rallis India (RALLIS): Q2 EBITDA falls to ₹126 Cr from ₹154 Cr; margin at 14.7%.

- Walchandnagar Industries (WALCHANNAG): NCLT admits insolvency plea against customer JUD Cements. Company sees no material incremental impact.

- Thirumalai Chemicals (TIRUMALCHM): Customs audit seeks ₹24.52 lakh RoDTEP repayment plus interest and penalty. Company disputes the demand.

- Elantas Beck India (ELANTAS): CFO Sanjay Kulkarni resigns effective October 21.

- Creative Eye (CREATIVEYE): CFO resigns effective November 14. Board approves ₹8 Cr overdraft and ₹8 Cr loan against property.

- Kross: EBITDA margin softens to 13% versus earlier 14–15% guidance. H2 revenue expected to grow 10–15% over H1.

- Banshali Engineering Polymers (BEPL): ABS 100k MTPA start-up guidance moves to March 2027 from September 2026.

NEUTRAL / CORPORATE ACTIONS

- Persistent Systems (PERSISTENT): QIP opens with ₹5,550 floor price; issue size up to $450 million (~₹4,265 Cr). ICRA also places ratings on Negative Implications watch.

- L&T Finance (LTF): Allots 1.5 lakh secured NCDs worth ₹1,500 Cr at 7.9% coupon, maturing September 2029. Option for 50,000 additional NCDs.

- Jubilant Pharmova (JUBLPHARMA): India Ratings assigns IND AA+/Stable to proposed ₹1,400 Cr NCDs.

- Eternal (ETERNAL): Q2 PAT rises 92% to ₹125 Cr; revenue grows 78%, but results miss estimates. Targets 3,500 stores by March 2027 and ~5,000 by March 2028. Stock closes down 2.5%.

- Gujarat Mineral Development Corporation (GMDCLTD): Presents ₹223.55 Cr dividend cheque to Gujarat Government. Total payout ₹302.1 Cr; FY26 final dividend ₹9.5/share.

- Shivam Autotech: Rights issue resized to ~₹120 Cr through 9.99 Cr shares at ₹12. Opens October 28; listing expected around November 25.

- Virtual Global Education: Approves ₹42 Cr preferential warrant issue and sale of Shikshan School subsidiary. CFO resigns; Krishan Bansal appointed CFO and Executive Director effective October 21.

- Advanced Enzyme Technologies (ADVENZYMES): Buys back 57,000 shares at ₹262.8 average (~₹1.5 Cr). Cumulative buyback reaches 21.43 lakh shares.

- Man Infraconstruction (MANINFRA): Buys back 1.3 lakh shares at ₹110.4 average (~₹1.4 Cr). Cumulative buyback reaches 99.2 lakh shares.

- Uno Minda (UNOMINDA): Targets ~₹40,000 Cr revenue by FY30 versus ₹19,700 Cr in FY26. Growth drivers include EV drives, seating, sunroofs and electronics.

- Cholamandalam Investment & Finance (CHOLAFIN): Board meets October 28 to consider a QIP or eligible convertible securities.

- ONGC: Government appoints Sunil Kumar Chairman for three years from December 7.

- Suryoday Small Finance Bank (SURYODAY): Approves raising up to ₹100 Cr through Lower Tier II NCDs.

- Nuvoco Vistas (NUVOCO): Targets 35 MMTPA cement capacity by FY28. Q2 affected by input costs, erratic rain and weak prices.

- Adani Total Gas (ATGL): Q2 revenue ₹2,102 Cr (+34%); PAT ₹167 Cr (+3%). Operates 723 CNG stations and serves 11.9 lakh PNG homes.

- CreditAccess Grameen (CREDITACC): Q2 PAT ₹501 Cr; NII ₹1,247 Cr. FY27 NIM guidance 14.4–14.7%; ROE guidance 21–24%.

- Adani Energy Solutions (ADANIENSOL): Metering business revenue potential reaches ₹29,519 Cr. About 24.6 million meters under implementation across 10 projects.

- Reliance Industries (RELIANCE): 7-Eleven closes its remaining 31 Indian stores, ending its five-year franchise tie-up with Reliance Retail.

- eMudhra (EMUDHRA): Exits global SSL/TLS certificate business to focus on enterprise and trust services.

- UGRO Capital (UGROCAP): NCLT Mumbai admits merger petition with Profectus Capital. Final hearing scheduled for November 20.

- SWELECT Energy Systems (SWELECTES): Acquires 100% of Sushma Solar Energy for up to ₹2.27 Cr cash. Plans a 50 MW group captive solar plant in Rajasthan.

- Apcotex Industries (APCOTEXIND): Buys 1.3% in Amplus Ampere from NRB Bearings for ₹72 lakh to support captive solar power.

- HFCL: Incorporates wholly owned subsidiary HFCL Connectivity Systems for technology and infrastructure services.

- Juniper Green Energy (JNPR): CARE assigns A+/Stable rating to ₹472.16 Cr long-term bank facilities of Juniper Green Spark Ten.

- Hi-Tech Pipes (HITECH): CRISIL reaffirms A+/Stable and A1 ratings on ₹565 Cr bank facilities.

- Elin Electronics (ELIN): CRISIL reaffirms A/Stable rating on ₹134 Cr bank facilities.

- S.H. Kelkar: Promoter pledge released.

- Swiggy: Lynks Logistics ceases to be a subsidiary of Swiggy Networks.

- Shriram Finance: To consider NCD and bond issuances on October 23.

- ESAF Small Finance Bank: Core banking migration scheduled for October 23–26.

- Bharat Electronics: Q2 results scheduled for October 30.

- Maharashtra Scooters / Bajaj Nivesh: Receives fresh certificate of incorporation following company name change.

- ITC: Q2 results scheduled for November 2.

- Vodafone Idea: Manoj Murali appointed Chief Operating Officer.

- AxisCades Technologies: Uttam Bhageria appointed CFO-Designate. Incorporates Indian arm Xponential Space for satellite, payload and allied space systems.

- Hindware Home: NCLT Kolkata sanctions demerger with HHIL.

- Bharat Coking Coal: Receives favourable High Court order; NGT disposes of mining case.

- L&T Technology Services (LTTS): Maintains mid-16% EBIT margin and 13–15% revenue CAGR guidance over the next 3–5 years.

- Waaree Renewable Technologies (WAAREERTL): Targets ₹5,500 Cr order book over the next 3–4 quarters. Maintains FY27 EBITDA margin objective above 15%.

- UltraTech Cement (ULTRACEMCO): Maintains ₹10,000 Cr FY27 capex and net debt/EBITDA below 1x by March 2027.

- Hindustan Zinc (HINDZINC): Maintains 680-tonne FY27 silver output target; mineral exploration completion guided for Q3 FY29.

- Gallantt Ispat (GALLANTT): Captive iron-ore benefit expected at ~₹2,000/tonne from FY28.

- Oriental Rail (ORIRAIL): Reports ₹1,692 Cr order book as of August 11, with an 18–22-month execution period.

- Jindal Saw (JINDALSAW): Order book including LOIs reaches ~₹16,200 Cr. Abu Dhabi DI backlog of $195 million provides 9–12 months' visibility.

- Bajaj Healthcare (BAJAJHCARE): Raises FY27 capex guidance to ₹65–80 Cr from ₹40–50 Cr. Maintains 10–15% revenue/PAT growth and 18–20% EBITDA margin guidance.

- Rossari Biotech (ROSSARI): Targets FY27-end export share above 30%, ~12% EBITDA margin and ~₹50 Cr H2 capex.

BULK / BLOCK DEALS

Significant Buys

- Adani Energy Solutions (ADANIENSOL): PI Opportunities AIF V buys 49.5 lakh shares at ₹1,334 (~₹661 Cr) from Prazim Trading.

- Manipal Health Enterprises (MANIPALHOS): PI Opportunities AIF V buys 19 lakh shares at ₹630 (~₹120 Cr) from Prazim Trading.

- Shriram Pistons & Rings (SHRIPISTON): PI Opportunities AIF V buys 2.57 lakh shares at ₹4,490 (~₹115 Cr) from Prazim Trading.

- Aditya Birla Capital (ABCAPITAL): PI Opportunities AIF V buys 30.7 lakh shares at ₹366 (~₹112 Cr) from Prazim Trading.

- HDFC Fire Protect (HDFIRE): Allianz buys 17.6 lakh shares at ₹317.48 (~₹56 Cr).

- Craftsman Automation (CRAFTSMAN): PI Opportunities AIF V buys 28,735 shares at ₹10,975 (~₹32 Cr) from Prazim Trading.

- Jindal Supreme (JSIPL): Neomile buys 10.8 lakh shares at ₹149.94 (~₹16 Cr).

- Gallantt Metal (GALLANTT): Suryalaxmi Infracon buys 26.52 lakh shares at ₹565 (~₹149.8 Cr) from Gallantt Industry Pvt Ltd. Related-party status requires verification.

- Capital Infra Trust (CAPINVIT): Larsen & Toubro buys 66.45 lakh units at ₹75.59 (~₹50.2 Cr) from A.K. Capital Finance.

Significant Sells

- Amir Chand Jagdish Kumar (AEROPLANE): Shlok Vimal Rathod sells 5.85 lakh shares at ₹209.59 (~₹12 Cr).

- Fusion CX (FUSIONCX): BNP Paribas Financial Markets sells 20.07 lakh shares at ₹303.91 and ₹304.81 (~₹61.1 Cr).

- Omni (OMNI): Junomoneta Finsol sells 8.31 lakh shares at ₹662 (~₹55 Cr).

PROMOTER / INSIDER ACTIVITY

Promoter / Insider Buys

- Afcom Holdings: Promoter Manjula Annamalai receives 10.5 lakh shares (3.7%) at ₹800 off-market from promoter Jaganmohan Manthena. Inter-se transfer; promoter-group holding unchanged.

- Sindhu Trade Links: Promoters Rudra Sen Sindhu and Vir Sen Sindhu receive 3.5% through a gift. Inter-se transfer among relatives; promoter-group holding remains 73.9%.

- Koura Fine Diamond Jewelry: Promoters acquire 2.2 lakh shares (3.5%) through preferential issue.

Pledge Updates

- Cineline India: Promoters release pledge on 65 lakh shares on October 19. Encumbered holding falls to zero.

- Deepak Builders and Engineers India: Pledges 20 lakh shares (0.5%) in favour of Comfort Fincap, a non-promoter entity.

KEY ITEMS TO TRACK

- BEL: Progress on the ₹30,000 Cr QRSAM order.
- NLC India: Thermal plant investment and project timelines.
- Coal India: Coal gasification project execution.
- Sagility: Chirok integration and growth after acquisition.
- Havells: Price hikes versus gross-margin recovery.
- HFCL: Execution of sharply raised revenue guidance.
- UltraTech Cement: EBITDA/tonne recovery and debt targets.
- Hindustan Zinc: Lower cost guidance and silver output.
- Persistent Systems: Rating-watch implications and QIP details.
- Yes Bank: Market reaction following the AT1 verdict.
- Adani Green Energy: Verification of reported grid-availability constraints.
- Swiggy: Path to profitability and growth delivery.
- Jindal Saw: Margin recovery following weak Q2 performance.
- Bajaj Healthcare: Higher capex and margin execution.
- Rossari Biotech: Export growth, margins and H2 capex.

Ola Electric – Goldman Sachs

• Rating: Downgraded to Sell

• Target Price: Cut to ₹23

• Goldman Sachs sees a more challenging path to free cash flow due to high interest costs, capex requirements and prolonged operating losses.

• Revenue needs to grow 3.6x–7.1x over FY26 levels by FY28–FY30 to cover current capex and interest obligations.

• Battery cell business faces potential operational challenges following the departure of its business head.

• FY27–FY29 revenue estimates cut by up to 10%, factoring in tougher market-share conditions versus two-wheeler peers.

• Key factors that could improve the outlook:
• Recovery in the electric two-wheeler business through a dealer-led sales and service model.

• Positive consolidated operating EBITDA margin.

• More customer wins and improved profitability in the battery cell business.

KEI Industries – HSBC

• Rating: Hold

• Target Price: Cut to ₹4,450

• Strong Q2FY27 revenue growth was overshadowed by weak margins, resulting in an earnings miss.

• Earnings growth is expected to remain strong, with a projected 20% EPS CAGR over FY26–FY29.

• Rising competition remains a key risk.

• Target price cut due to lower earnings forecasts.

KEI Industries – CLSA

• Rating: Upgraded to Outperform

• Target Price: Cut to ₹4,845

• CLSA believes competition risks and the marginal guidance cut are largely factored in after the recent stock correction.

• Q2FY27 PAT came in slightly below estimates despite strong revenue growth due to lower margins.

• FY27 revenue growth guidance maintained at 25%, with volume growth guidance of 10%+.

• EBITDA margin guidance is expected to be at the lower end of the earlier 11–12% range.

• Capacity expansion supports medium-term growth of 20%+.

• Competitive and supply-side risks appear largely priced in, according to CLSA.

CreditAccess Grameen – HSBC

• Rating: Buy

• Target Price: Cut to ₹1,400

• Profitability, currently well above through-the-cycle levels, is expected to normalise going forward.

• HSBC cut EPS estimates by 3.6–4.9% for FY27–FY28, factoring in lower AUM growth in FY27, fee compression and higher provisions.

• Target price cut as the cyclical downturn deepens.

• Despite near-term challenges, HSBC believes the current market price offers value.
STOCK TO WATCH

CreditAccess Grameen – CLSA

• Rating: Outperform

• Target Price: Cut to ₹1,600

• Q2FY27 PPOP beat estimates by 7%, driven by better NII.

• PAT remained in line with estimates due to the creation of a macroprudential buffer.

• Management raised FY27 ROA guidance by around 100 bps after ROA exceeded guidance for the second consecutive quarter.

• AUM growth accelerated to 19%, led by retail finance, which accounts for around 25% of AUM and continues to report lower delinquencies.

• Net slippages rose around 70 bps QoQ but remain below steady-state levels.

• Management expects some increase in credit costs in Q3FY27 due to drought conditions.

• CLSA cut FY28–FY29 PAT estimates by 2–4%, factoring in another repo rate hike and the impact of draft insurance distribution guidelines.

Havells India – Jefferies

• Rating: Hold

• Target Price: ₹1,220

• September quarter sales surged 35% YoY, driven by Cables & Wires (copper price pass-through) and double-digit volume growth in switchgears.

• Low base in the room air conditioner (RAC) segment also supported growth.

• PAT grew 11% YoY, in line with Jefferies' estimates, as other income declined sharply due to a one-off gain in the previous year.

• Operating margin remained firm at 9%, supported by price hikes of around 10–15% over the past 12 months.

**MORGAN STANLEY ON ADANI GREEN**

- Recommendation: Overweight | Target: ₹1,525

- Strong Q2 beat: revenue +2%, EBITDA +8% versus estimates.

- Strong PAT performance followed the EBITDA beat.

- Wind and hybrid CUFs significantly exceeded expectations year-on-year.

- Key monitorables: merchant realisations, BESS contribution and FY27 scale-up.

- Curtailment impact remains an important monitorable.

**MORGAN STANLEY ON VISHAL MEGA MART**

- Recommendation: Overweight | Target: ₹146

- Broad-based miss; festive timing impact exceeded expectations.

- FY27 double-digit SSSG target reiterated.

- Lower Q2 growth is expected to be offset in Q3.

- No customer demand moderation observed across regions.

- Current inflation levels require no further price hikes.

- Cost re-engineering should support FY27 margin stability.

- Advances growth FY27: 18–20%, raised from 16–18%.
- Q2 advances growth: 19.3%.
- Deposit growth FY27: 13–14%, kept.
- Q2 deposit growth: 13.0%.
- Gross NPA by Mar-27: <2%, kept.
- Q2 Gross NPA: 2.09%.

**Yes Bank** — Kept
- RoA FY27 exit: ~1%, kept.
- Guidance partly based on non-core.
- Stock -3.5% after Q1.

**Union Bank** — New
- Written-off recovery FY27: ~₹3,000 Cr target.
- Target based on H1 run-rate.
- Capital raise FY27: ₹8,000 Cr.
- Capital raise is board-approved.

**Bajaj Finance** — Kept
- New customers FY27: 18–20 million.
- Gold-loan branches FY27: 2,700–2,800.
- Opex/NTI FY27 improvement: 25–40 bps, new.
- Stock +8.9% after Q1.
- Q2 call pending.

**Piramal Finance** — Kept
- AUM growth FY27: 25%.
- Q2 AUM growth: 24%.
- PAT growth FY27: 50%.
- RoAUM exit Q4: 2.5%.
- Q2 RoAUM: 2.0%.

**M&M Financial** — Kept
- Loan growth: 16–18%, medium term.
- Core growth: +21%.
- RoA: 2.2–2.5%.
- H1 RoA: 2.3%.
- Credit cost FY27: 1.3–1.7%.
- Stock +16.6% after Q1.

**Aye Finance** — Kept
- AUM growth FY27: 25–30%.
- Q2 growth: 26.0%.
- Credit cost FY27: 3.5–4.0%.
- Q2 credit cost: 3.82%.
- RoTA FY27: 4.0–4.5%.
- Q2 RoTA: 4.04%.
- Q2 call pending.

**TELECOM & TECH**

**HFCL** — Raised
- Revenue growth FY27: ≥80%.
- Earlier guidance was ~40%.
- ₹10,000 Cr revenue target: Pre-FY29.
- Earlier target was by FY29.
- Defence revenue FY27: ~₹500 Cr, kept.
- Revenue guidance raised twice: 20% → 40% → 80%.

**L&T Technology Services (LTTS)** — Kept
- EBIT margin: Mid-16%.
- Q2 EBIT margin: 16.3%.
- Revenue CAGR: 13–15% over next 3–5 years.
- Long-term EBIT margin: 16–17%.
- Stock +7.0% after Q1.

**Waaree Renewable** — Kept
- Order book to revenue: ₹5,500 Cr, new.
- Conversion expected over next 3–4 quarters.
- EBITDA margin FY27: >15%, kept.
- Objective approximately 15%.
- Stock -8.0% after Q1.

**CONSUMER & LEISURE**

**Indian Hotels (INDHOTEL)** — Raised
- Revenue growth FY27: 15–17%.
- Earlier guidance: 12–14%.
- H1 revenue growth: ~18%.
- Portfolio target: 700 hotels before Mar-27.
- Earlier target was by 2030.
- Current portfolio: ~390 hotels.
- Hotel segment FY27 growth: 17–19%, new.

**Vishal Mega Mart (VMM)** — Raised
- FY27 store openings: >100.
- Earlier guidance: 80–100.
- FY27 SSSG: ≥10%, new.
- Q3 requires >10% SSSG.
- Stock -4.8% after Q1.

**Mahindra Holidays (MHRIL)** — Kept
- Gross key additions FY27: ~1,000.
- Expected over next two quarters.
- Room inventory FY30: 10,000 keys.
- 85% of funnel visible.
- Stock -4.0% after Q1.

**IGI (International Gemological Institute)** — Raised
- Revenue growth FY27: ~27%.
- Earlier guidance: ~15%, "like H1".
- H1 revenue growth: +27%.
- EBITDA growth FY27: ~34%.
- Earlier guidance: ~20%, "like H1".
- H1 EBITDA growth: +34%.
- FY27 expected to track H1.

**Eternal** — Kept
- Blinkit NOV/store/day: ~₹11 lakh.
- Steady-state guidance maintained.
- Margins guided flattish for 1–2 years.

**PC Jeweller** — New
- Large-format showrooms: Up to 100.
- Timeline: Next 12–18 months.
- First openings guided this FY.

**REALTY**

**Sobha** — Kept
- Pre-sales growth FY27: ≥30%.
- Management hopes to exceed guidance.
- H1 pre-sales growth: +47%.
- PAT growth FY27: ≥50%, new.
- EBITDA margin: ~20%+, new.
- Margin expected to stabilise from H2.
- Q2 EBITDA margin: 11%.

**Marathon Nextgen** — New
- Pre-sales FY27: >₹1,000 Cr.
- FY26 pre-sales: ~₹1,000 Cr.
- Inventory to launch: ~₹10,000 Cr.
- Launch pipeline over next five years.
- No Q2 call yet.

**CEMENT, METALS & INDUSTRIALS**

**UltraTech Cement** — Kept
- EBITDA/tonne target: ₹1,400.
- Target timeline: Exit FY28.
- FY27 capex: ₹10,000 Cr.
- Net debt/EBITDA Mar-27: <1x.
- September net debt/EBITDA: 1.26x.
- Stock +3.1% after Q1.

**Hindustan Zinc** — Raised
- Zinc cost FY27: $825–850/tonne.
- Earlier guidance: $975–1,000/tonne.
- Q2 zinc cost: $703/tonne.
- Silver output FY27: 680 tonnes, kept.
- H1 silver output: 321 tonnes.
- Mineral exploration completion: Q3 FY29, new.
- Lower cost guidance supports better margins.

**Gallantt Ispat** — Kept
- New-capacity utilisation: 85–90%, new.
- Expected within ~6 weeks.
- Captive iron-ore gain: ~₹2,000/tonne.
- Benefit expected from FY28.
- Iron-ore blocks live: FY28, kept.
- Stock +15.8% after Q1.

**Kross Ltd** — Mixed
- EBITDA margin: 14–15%, softened.
- Q2 EBITDA margin: 13%.
- No timeline for margin target now.
- Export growth FY27: +45%, kept.
- H2 vs H1 revenue: +10–15%, new.
- Stock -5.0% after Q1.

**LMW** — New
- Unit III capacity addition: +125/month.
- Expected by December 2026.
- Current utilisation: 90%.
- Unit III capex: ₹10 Cr.
- Capex funded through internal accruals.

**ORDER BOOKS**

**Swastika Infra** — New
- FY27-end order book: ~₹2,000 Cr.
- Guided range: ₹1,500–2,000 Cr.
- Current order book: ₹1,420 Cr.
- July order book: ₹916 Cr.
- Current order book: 2.8x FY26 revenue.
- Q2 order win: ~₹600 Cr.
- Execution skewed toward Q3–Q4.

**Oriental Rail** — New
- Order book as of 11 Aug: ₹1,692 Cr.
- Equivalent to ~3x FY26 revenue.
- Execution period: 18–22 months.
- No Q2 call yet.

**Jindal Saw** — New
- Order book including LOIs: ~₹16,200 Cr.
- Subject to LOI conversion.
- Abu Dhabi DI backlog: $195 million.
- Backlog visibility: 9–12 months.
- H2 margins guided better than H1.

**PHARMA & CHEMICALS**

**Bajaj Healthcare** — Raised
- FY27 capex: ₹65–80 Cr.
- Earlier capex guidance: ₹40–50 Cr.
- Revenue & PAT growth FY27: 10–15%.
- H1 growth: +15%.
- EBITDA margin FY27: 18–20%.
- Q2 EBITDA margin: 18.2%.
- Stock -13.5% after Q1.

**Rossari Biotech** — Kept
- Export share FY27-end: 30%+, new.
- Q2 export share: 31%.
- EBITDA margin FY27: ~12%, new.
- Capex H2 FY27: ~₹50 Cr, new.

**Bhansali Engineering Polymers (BEPL)** — Cut
- ABS 100k MTPA start: March 2027.
- Earlier target: September 2026.
- Reactor expected November 2026.

**GUIDANCE STATUS**
- Raised: PSB, HFCL, Indian Hotels, VMM, IGIL, Hindustan Zinc, Bajaj Healthcare.
- Cut: BEPL.
- Mixed: Kross.
- Several companies maintained existing guidance.
- Multiple companies introduced fresh targets.

- Non-fluorochemicals businesses dragged performance.

- Consolidated gross margin declined due to raw material inflation and softer sequential demand.

- Chemicals performance was broadly in line, supported by strong refrigerant sales.

.

- Food-delivery margins are flattening.

- Specialty Chemicals EBIT suffered from margin pressure.

- Refrigerant gases continued their strong performance.

- Packaging Films and Technical Textiles EBIT missed expectations.

- Mazagon Dock: Initiate Sell; target price ₹1,855.

- Garden Reach Shipbuilders: Initiate Sell; target price ₹1,515.

- Mazagon Dock faces low book-to-bill and long project gestation.

- Garden Reach earnings may decline as key NGC orders get delayed.

**JEFFERIES ON INDIA STRATEGY**

- Organised sector employment growth moderates.
- Job creation hit a five-year low of 1.8% YoY in FY26.
- Hiring moderated across most sectors, particularly financials.
- Estimated salary hikes improved to 9.4%.

Curious when FII will come back to India

So gave Co-pilot a prompt
“Why FIIs wont return to India even as AI trade unwind globally”

Reverse Psychology

Here is the response

1. India is still expensive vs EM peers
o Even after corrections, India trades at a premium to most emerging markets.
o FIIs compare India with China, Korea, Taiwan, Brazil, not with India's own history.
o If China is at 10-12x PE and India at 20-25x PE, capital tends to chase cheaper markets. 
2. India lacks direct AI beneficiaries
o The AI trade created winners in US tech, Taiwan semiconductors and Korean memory-chip companies.
o India has very few large listed AI, semiconductor or hyperscaler plays that global thematic funds can buy. 
3. Dollar returns matter, not rupee returns
o FIIs think in USD.
o Even if Nifty is flat or slightly up, rupee depreciation can wipe out returns.
o Currency risk remains a major deterrent for foreign capital. 
4. US yields remain a strong competitor
o If US Treasuries offer attractive risk-free returns, FIIs need a much higher expected return from India.
o Many global allocators prefer earning 4-5% in dollar assets rather than taking EM risk. 
5. India's earnings growth has moderated
o India's premium valuation was justified when earnings were compounding rapidly.
o If earnings growth slows while valuations remain rich, FIIs question the risk-reward. 
6. Better opportunities elsewhere
o Korea, Taiwan and China offer exposure to AI, semiconductors and manufacturing at lower valuations.
o Global funds have finite capital; India is competing against these markets for allocation. 
7. India is no longer an under-owned market
o After years of strong inflows, most EM funds already have meaningful India exposure.
o Incremental flows require a new catalyst, not just the absence of AI enthusiasm.
8. Domestic flows reduce urgency
o SIPs, mutual funds and insurance money continue supporting Indian markets despite FII selling.
o Paradoxically, this resilience prevents large valuation corrections that would otherwise attract FIIs back.

Maruti Suzuki India should be rechristened as Suzuki India

Maruti's journey started as a Govt of India project. Maruti Udyog was the Indian promoter & Suzuki was brought in as the technology partner. Back then, this was very much an Indian company with Japanese know-how.

Over time, the Indian promoter gradually diluted its holding & eventually exited completely. Suzuki did the opposite, staying invested through every cycle & steadily increasing its stake.

What began as a JV slowly became Suzuki's most important global asset. The ownership story itself tells you who has deepened commitment over the decades.

For years, investors debated why Suzuki was setting up fresh manufacturing capacity outside Maruti Suzuki through its Gujarat subsidiary instead of housing it directly in the listed entity.

Then came the reversal. Suzuki transferred Suzuki Motor Gujarat into Maruti Suzuki at a valuation of roughly ₹12,000+ Cr. Rather than taking cash, it largely took equity.

The result? Suzuki's ownership in Maruti Suzuki moved up further without having to buy equivalent shares from the secondary market.

This wasn't just a restructuring exercise. It was Suzuki effectively converting manufacturing assets into a larger stake in India's largest PV company.

Even after that transaction, Suzuki did not stop. It has periodically picked up additional shares from the open market whenever opportunities emerged.

The message is clear. The Indian promoter exited long ago. The Japanese promoter keeps doubling down on India.

Look at the cars on the road today. The branding emphasis is on the giant "S" logo. 10-15years back, cars started selling with only “S” logo, 1st on premium nexa cars, then on all the models. You will hardly see Maruti branded cars on road now

For many younger buyers, the brand recall is shifting from "Maruti Suzuki" to simply "Suzuki". The transition is subtle but visible.

India is now the crown jewel of Suzuki Motor Corp. A substantial portion of Suzuki valuation come from Indian listed entity. Maruti $38bn mcap translate to $21bn (for 58% stake, $15bn if applied 30% Holdco disc).

Even beyond that, Maruti pays over $500m to Suzuki as royalty, that value must be over $5bn in the SoTP of Suzuki motors. Suzuki motors also have successful 2w biz in India, they are 6th largest 2w in India, clocking over 1lac units every month

In many ways, investors buying Suzuki Motor Corp are indirectly buying the India story. Cars sold by Suzuki in India is higher than overall car sold by Suzuki in other 100 countries combined

A rebranding to "Suzuki India" could also help shed the old "cheap small-car company" perception. As premium SUVs, hybrids & future EVs gain share, a stronger global MNC identity may command a different customer mindset.

Ownership, capital allocation, manufacturing integration, branding & growth strategy all point in one direction: this is increasingly Suzuki's India story.

Conclusion: Maruti only stays in Co. name hence should be renamed now

What regulators see that investors often ignore 👇

Every time a regulator acts, investors first ask: "How much EPS gets hit?" Regulators ask something else: "Is the market structure fair for the end consumer?" That's a very different lens. 
Thoughts on recent #PBFintech & older #IEX n more

Case in point: Recent change on insurance commissions. The proposed changes effectively aim to reduce distribution costs & curb excessive upfront payouts on some products. Investors see lower margins. Regulators see lower customer acquisition costs & better value for policyholders.

Truth is, hardly anyone argues that insurance has zero mis-selling. Higher upfront commissions have often created incentives to sell what pays the most, not what suits the customer best. If that problem exists, intervention shouldn't be surprising.

The irony is that many investors celebrate efficiency in every industry except their own portfolio holdings. When a regulator targets excess distribution costs, the reaction is often outrage instead of introspection.

Look at insurance expense ratios. Even as the industry scaled up, commission/expense pools as a % of premium remained elevated in several segments. The regulator's job is to ask: why isn't scale translating into lower customer costs?

Learning from MFs TER. Every TER cut was seen as fatal attack. Prediction was: growth will die, distributors will vanish, profit collapse. Instead industry adapted. Players became efficient, direct plans gained share, technology reduced costs, investor participation & AUM surged

Market coupling in power exch. Investors focus: which exchange lose market share. Regulators focus: consumers get better price discovery. Market coupling means bids/orders from all exch get pooled to discover a single price. One price improves efficiency & reduces fragmentation

Could one exchange lose moat? Maybe. But from system perspective, better price discovery, deeper liquidity & lower market distortion are hard to ignore.
Regulators rarely optimize for shareholder returns. They optimize for consumers, market efficiency & long-term public interest

Think about hospitals. If tomorrow there is stricter price regulation, hospital stocks may get hit. As investors we'd feel the pain. But can anyone honestly deny healthcare costs are becoming unaffordable for a large section of Indians?
One may argue India's healthcare is still cheaper than many countries. True. But the person comparing prices globally is not the same person struggling to pay a hospital bill locally.

Markets often assume regulators must protect industry profitability. Regulators believe industries shouldn't fleece poor customers. When public benefit & industry profits collide, the regulator's choice is usually obvious.

That's why stock market reaction is often the last variable in the regulator's decision. If a policy improves consumer outcomes, transparency, affordability or efficiency, temporary shareholder pain rarely changes the outcome.
